title: MyRecon vs DeHashed: OSINT & Breach Workflows Compared
description: Compare MyRecon and DeHashed: search inputs, breach workflows and verification limits. Choose an OSINT tool for authorized research.
h1: MyRecon vs DeHashed: compare breach and footprint workflows
intro: Compare DeHashed and MyRecon by the question you need to answer. DeHashed describes indexed exposure research; MyRecon helps review public username candidates and supported exposure checks. This comparison does not establish superior accuracy or complete coverage.

sections.heading: What DeHashed documents
sections.body: DeHashed documents searches across collected exposure data using inputs such as usernames, emails and IP addresses. It also describes monitoring, an API and historical WHOIS services. These are provider descriptions, not results of our own comparative trial.

sections.heading: What MyRecon checks and what a result means
sections.body: MyRecon checks public usernames across a supported catalogue of 500+ platforms. The chosen scan scope determines which checks run. Found means a lead for source review. Not found does not guarantee registration availability. Unknown means the check could not reach a reliable conclusion. Email and password-exposure tools are separate checks, not a complete inventory of every account.

sections.heading: Illustrative decision: Historical exposure versus a current profile
sections.body: For your own address appearing in an exposure record, note the incident and take account-security action. To check a known public handle, inspect the current profile URL separately. Historical records cannot establish that an account is still active or that a password still works.

sections.heading: Access and costs before you choose
sections.body: MyRecon guest Quick scans show a limited preview. Standard scans require sign-in; account and plan limits apply. Paid features are described on the current pricing page. Check DeHashed provider terms and available fields separately. This page does not claim either service is unlimited, always free or anonymous, and includes no paid-account or same-scope benchmark.

sections.heading: Record evidence and verify your next action
sections.body: For each authorized check, record the exact input, date, scope, result status and source URL. Keep unknown outcomes separate from negative results. Confirm accounts you own through an existing login or official recovery process, apply the privacy or security change, and recheck the specific exposure. A shared username alone does not identify a person.

faq.question: Is MyRecon a direct replacement for DeHashed?
faq.answer: It depends on the task. Public profile discovery and indexed exposure research have different inputs and evidence limits. Compare the required workflow before switching.

faq.question: Can I try MyRecon for free?
faq.answer: Guest Quick scans offer a limited preview. Standard scans require sign-in, and account and plan limits apply. See the current pricing page.

faq.question: Does a match prove ownership?
faq.answer: No. A shared username, similar name or historical record is not ownership proof. Keep uncertain matches unconfirmed and review independent evidence.
